gap: No result ChatGPT got states a dollar price for any model. On 2026-11-10 GardePro's US store listed both home-Wi-Fi picks, the E8 3.0 Pro and E9 3.0 Pro, at $119.99. The near-identical E8 2.0 Pro sells for $99.99 and its listing says it is 'Unable to connect to home router'.
standout_why: I compared against the cited magnoliatrailcamera.com/best-wifi-trail-camera page and the uncited lenstroop.com, itechguides.com (Wi-Fi guide) and dognotebook.com roundups. Magnolia, Lenstroop and Dognotebook give no dollar figures (only 'Check Price' links or labels like 'Budget Pick'). Itechguides prices only phone-hotspot cameras (MAXDONE $53.99/$50.99, GardePro E6 $59.99), none of which join a router. None of these pages price the E8 3.0 Pro, the E9 3.0 Pro or the Link 1.0, and none points out that GardePro's cheaper, similarly named E8 2.0 / E8 2.0 Pro / E6 2.0 cannot join home Wi-Fi.
decides: Confirms ChatGPT's pick but changes how to frame it. The E8 3.0 Pro and E9 3.0 Pro cost the same ($119.99), so on the maker's store price alone neither is cheaper. The real money trap is the $20 cheaper E8 2.0 Pro ($99.99) and the $84.99 E6 2.0, whose listings say they cannot connect to a home router. For a camera within router range, the answer is 'E8 3.0 Pro or E9 3.0 Pro at $119.99, and don't buy anything with 2.0 in the name'. GardePro's E8 3.0 Pro overview says neither home-Wi-Fi model offers Live View in Home WiFi Mode. The Link 1.0 adds remote live view and hub range for far placements, but I could not confirm its hub-plus-camera bundle price today.
